name: AppLovin
key_signal: APP has fallen 43% from its 52-week high and trades below both its 50- and 200-day moving averages with decisively negative momentum across the 21d, 63d, and 126d windows.
thesis: AppLovin remains a highly profitable growth engine—59% revenue growth, 78% operating margin, 64% net margin, and 113% earnings growth—with a forward P/E of just ~19.6x that looks cheap relative to its growth profile, and the 30-analyst consensus still rates it strong buy, suggesting the recent drawdown may eventually be viewed as a valuation reset rather than a fundamental impairment.
bear_case: The technical picture is unambiguously deteriorating: price is below both the 50-day (505) and 200-day (532) moving averages with no golden cross, momentum is negative on every horizon (-17.6% 1M, -8.9% 3M, -31.3% 6M), MACD histogram is sharply negative, and RSI at 36 shows room to fall further before oversold—this is a stock in a confirmed downtrend, not consolidation. Combined with a beta of 2.48 and 73% annualized volatility, any broader market weakness or continued deceleration in mobile ad spend will amplify losses; meanwhile the trailing P/E of 37x and price-to-book of 60x (against a debt/equity of 163%) leave little margin for error if growth decelerates from its current elevated pace, and the stock has already round-tripped from 745 to the low 400s once sentiment shifted, showing how quickly the market re-rates this name when momentum breaks.
